subject: Marius: lopsided-gated fits not more predictive (m1/m3/m4)
body: Results in experiments/lopsided_all/pref_results.json. Fitting Gio's m1/m3/m4 on only the 94 weak-gated pre-T pairs (vs all 273) makes them worse on all 100 pre-T dev pairs (m4 -0.21, m1 -0.10, m3 -0.07) and no better on all 83 held-out pairs. Gains on gated test subsets are circular: the gate keeps pairs where he went against a generic Haiku judge, so gated fits learn contrarianism. Also: m0 (Haiku, no history) picks his option 63% on pre-T dev but 34% on held-out, so his post-T choices mostly go against the generic default (or the post-T pairs favour the distractor). m2/m5 pass running next.
